Simulate a fictional lost-sales inventory system exactly. There is no stochastic prediction and no missing information beyond the explicit reporting cutoff.
Receipts add quantity to stock. Demands consume min(stock, quantity); any unmet quantity is lost (never backlogged). A stockout means strictly positive unmet demand, not merely ending with zero stock.
For raw report histories: first keep reports with received_time <= knowledge_cutoff. Then choose the highest visible revision for EACH event_id. Revisions REPLACE earlier reports, not add to them. Then keep chosen events with event_time <= target_time. Apply these events in (event_time, event_id) order, starting from initial_stock. Ignore any report not visible at the knowledge cutoff even if its event occurred earlier. Arrival order is not event order.
The canonical arm supplies the already selected eligible events in event-time order. The snapshot arm supplies the exactly replayed historical state. These are explicitly identified, executable preprocessing interventions.
After the historical reconstruction, apply every event in the given future_schedule in (event_time, event_id) order from the reconstructed stock. This is an explicitly known hypothetical scenario, not privileged knowledge about a real future.
Return five integers through submit_answer: stock_at_target; total historical_lost through target_time using visible revisions; stock_at_horizon after the scenario; future_lost for the scenario ONLY; first_future_stockout_time, the earliest future scenario event time with unmet demand, or -1 if no future demand is unmet. Do not count historical stockouts in that last field.

The problem has many steps: 1) filter reports with received_time <= knowledge_cutoff. 2) For each event_id, choose the highest visible revision (i.e., the one with maximal revision number among those with received_time <= cutoff). Revisions replace earlier reports instead of adding. 3) Then keep chosen events with event_time <= target_time. 4) Apply these events in (event_time, event_id) order, starting from initial_stock. 5) The stock after processing all events up to target_time is the "stock_at_target". Additionally we need to compute total historical_lost through target_time using visible revisions. Lost is defined as unmet demand: when demand > stock, you consume min(stock, quantity) i.e., all available stock, then the unmet quantity is lost and never backlogged. A stockout is strictly positive unmet demand (i.e., when demand > stock at that moment). That might be used for the field "first_future_stockout_time", but historical lost counting includes all lost (unmet) amounts across the historical events up to target_time.

Next we must apply the future schedule events (the given list), after the historical reconstruction is done, to the inventory from that reconstructed stock state. We need to apply every event in future_schedule in (event_time, event_id) order, including the original event_id ordering if they have same event_time (but they have unique IDs). The future schedule is "explicitly known hypothetical scenario", not privileged knowledge.

We need to compute final stock after processing all future events up to horizon_time? The horizon_time is defined as an input parameter = 130. The problem states: Return five integers: stock_at_target; total historical_lost through target_time using visible revisions; stock_at_horizon after the scenario; future_lost for the scenario ONLY; first_future_stockout_time, the earliest future scenario event time with unmet demand, or -1 if no future demand is unmet. Do not count historical stockouts in that last field.

So after processing all future events (including the receipt at 130), we compute stock_at_horizon.

Also compute future_lost: sum of unmet demand in future schedule events only (i.e., lost quantity for those events, ignoring historical lost). And first_future_stockout_time: earliest event_time (in future) where unmet demand >0 (i.e., a stockout). If none, -1.
